title: Screen readers hear a two-page spread left page first: the book DOM is in page-flip (reversed) order
evidence: flip.loadFromHTML([...elements].reverse()) (PdfBookReader.tsx:310) makes page-flip append the leaves in reversed order (t1.json domOrder: back, endpaper, blank, end, page5, page4, page3, ...). Each page leaf carries its spoken text (pdf.ts:138-146). At the spread 3-4 at 1440 (t1.json srOrder): page 4 at x=158 (left) comes before page 3 at x=720 (right) in DOM, and the group ariaSnapshot (t1.json aria34) reads «صورة الروضة وبين الذاكرة...» (page 4) before «وكان لكل بيتٍ رائحةٌ...» (page 3). Screenshot t1-spread34-1440.png shows page 3 on the right.
impact: Every screen-reader user on a screen wide enough for two pages (container >= 800px) who reads the open book in browse mode hears each spread in the wrong order: the left page (read second in an Arabic book) before the right one, e.g. the start of «صورة الروضة» before the end of «المقدمة». WCAG 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (A). The reading view (StaticPdfReader) is in the right order; portrait shows one leaf.
proposed_fix: Take the spoken text out of the leaves: drop the visually-hidden div in PageSurface (pdf.ts:138-146) for the book and render, in React next to the host, one visually-hidden block with referenceText() of the shown pages in reading order (shown.map(i => leaves[i]) filtered to pages). Alternatively set aria-owns on the group listing the spoken divs ids in reading order.
prior_overlap: none (AUDIT-1/2 checked the spoken text exists, not its order)

title: On touch screens a scroll that starts on the book turns a page, and a slow tap turns two
evidence: page-flip 2.0.7 (node_modules/page-flip/src/UI/UI.ts onTouchStart/onTouchEnd) arms a press 250ms after touchstart (startUserTouch) and, at touchend, calls userStop(pos,false), which runs flipController.flip(pos) whenever the finger did not fold the page. mobileScrollSupport: true (PdfBookReader.tsx:307) lets the browser scroll but never disarms that press, and the reader only intercepts mouseup (lines 403-415). CDP touch runs against the export (t2.mjs/t2.json phone 360x780 DPR3; t3.mjs/t3.json tablet 1024x768): a 450ms upward scroll starting on the left of the page scrolled the page 183px AND turned 4/5 -> 5/5; the same scroll downward on the right half turned 5/5 -> 4/5; on the tablet a scroll turned 1/5 -> 2/5. A 350ms tap on the left quarter turned twice (phone: 2/5 -> 3/5 -> 4/5, page-flip at touchend plus the reader turn queued from the compat mouseup; tablet: 1/5 -> 3-4/5 -> 5/5). A 60ms tap turns once.
impact: On phones, where the book fills about half the screen (320x400 of 360x780), most deliberate scrolls start on it: a visitor scrolling past the preview or towards the toolbar sees the book turn a page each time, and a slightly slow tap skips a page. Reading the approved pages on the most common device is erratic; no data or money at stake.
proposed_fix: In the build effect, add one window touchend listener in the capture phase (it runs before page-flip own window touchend): unless page-flip is folding (stateRef.current is user_fold or fold_corner), call flip.userStop({x:0,y:0}, true) so page-flip forgets the press; quick swipes still turn through page-flip own swipe branch and taps through the compat mouse events (portrait via onRelease, landscape via page-flip click). Remove it in releaseListeners. Add an e2e with CDP touch: a 450ms vertical scroll on the book and a 350ms tap each change the label at most once.
prior_overlap: none: P02 audit-2 C1/C2 fixed mouse clicks only; the e2e phone test taps the toolbar button, never the page

title: Once opened, the book keeps the main thread about half busy on a phone, at rest and scrolled away, until the visitor leaves /book
evidence: page-flip Render.start() runs requestAnimationFrame forever while the book exists, and every frame HTMLRender.drawFrame() rewrites style.cssText on every leaf (clear() sets display:none on each hidden leaf, simpleDraw() rewrites the shown ones; node_modules/page-flip/src/Render/HTMLRender.ts:326-366). The pnpm patch only stops the loop on destroy(). Measured on the export (t5.json idle: 854 style mutations/s and 61 rAF/s at rest; 60 rAF/s with the book 3815px below the viewport). t6.mjs/t6.json, 360x780 DPR3, CPU throttled x4, 5 s windows: book closed TaskDuration 5 ms, RecalcStyleCount 0; book open at rest TaskDuration 2796 ms, 312 style recalcs (1238 ms), script 376 ms; scrolled to the top of the page, book off screen: TaskDuration 2629 ms, 302 recalcs.
impact: A phone visitor who opens the preview and then keeps reading /book (photos, journey, editions) carries a 60fps style-recalc loop that takes about 53% of a mid-range phone main thread: battery drain, a warm phone, and janky scrolling and reveals for the rest of the page, until they navigate away.
proposed_fix: Run the loop only when it has work. Smallest step: in the build effect, observe the host with an IntersectionObserver and stop page-flip loop while the book is off screen (set the patched render.stopped flag via flip.getRender(), and on re-entry clear it and call getRender().start()). Better, extend patches/page-flip@2.0.7.patch so the loop calls drawFrame() only while an animation runs, the state is not read, or after update()/a page change; keep the destroy stop. Prove with the Performance metrics above (closed vs open at rest).
prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S15.2 fixed the loop surviving destroy(); the loop cost while the book is mounted was not covered

title: Keyboard focus falls to <body> when the focused «النسخ ←» link turns away with an arrow key
evidence: onKeyDown (PdfBookReader.tsx:490-497) turns the book whatever element inside the group has focus. The end leaf link lives in a page-flip leaf, which page-flip hides with display:none once it leaves the spread. t4.mjs endLeafKeys at 1440: End, then Tab -> focus A «النسخ ←»; ArrowLeft -> the book turns to [blank|endpaper] and document.activeElement is BODY (t4.json afterArrowLeft: "BODY:انتقل إلى المحتوى..."). Further arrows do nothing, since the keydown handler is on the group.
impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user who tabs onto «النسخ ←» and then keeps turning with the arrows loses focus to the top of the document; the next Tab restarts from the skip link and the next arrow press does nothing.
proposed_fix: In onKeyDown, before turning, move focus back to the group when the key came from inside a leaf: if (event.target !== event.currentTarget) event.currentTarget.focus({ preventScroll: true }).

title: Opening the book drops keyboard focus to <body> while it loads, and a first failure leaves it there
evidence: BookPreview swaps its whole tree for <PdfBookReader> once the chunk arrives, unmounting the pressed «افتح الكتاب». The focus effect only runs for retries: if (attempt > 0 && !loaded) (failed ? retryRef : statusRef).current?.focus() (PdfBookReader.tsx:183-185). t4.json: slow PDF (2.5 s delay) -> during loading activeElement is BODY; blocked PDF -> after the first «تعذّر فتح الصفحات.» activeElement is BODY ("BODY:انتقل إلى المحتوى..."); after a retry it is the retry button (the AUDIT-2 FIX-public-8 path).
impact: A keyboard user who opens the book on a slow connection, or whose first load fails, is left on <body>; the failure is announced (role=alert) but the retry button is not focused, unlike every later attempt.
proposed_fix: Drop the attempt > 0 condition: if (!loaded) (failed ? retryRef : statusRef).current?.focus(), so the first load focuses the loading status and a first failure focuses «إعادة المحاولة».
prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S15.3 and AUDIT-2 FIX-public-8 fixed the retry paths only (attempt > 0)

title: Going from two pages to one (rotating a tablet, narrowing the window) lands on the left page and skips the right one
evidence: page-flip keeps its own current index, which in the reversed book is the left (later) page of a spread; on the switch to portrait its update() fires flip with that index and the handler (PdfBookReader.tsx:333-351) just shows it. t4.json resize: at 1440 on «3–4 / 5», resized to 700 -> «4 / 5» (page 4 alone); on «5 / 5» ([5 | end]) -> «نهاية الصفحات المتاحة» (the end leaf), page 5 skipped.
impact: A reader on a tablet who rotates to portrait while reading the right-hand page (page 3, or page 5, the last page of the preview) is moved one page ahead and must go back to finish it.
proposed_fix: On changeOrientation to portrait, take the right leaf of the landscape spread (visibleLeaves(indexRef.current, total, false)[0]) before the update and, when it is not empty and differs from the shown leaf, go() to it once the orientation event has been handled.
prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 BOOK-3 (portrait from the last, empty spread) is fixed; this is the spreads with text on the right

title: In full screen, «عرض للقراءة» opens on the bottom of page 3: the tools and pages 1-3 are above the scroll origin and cannot be reached
evidence: .reader:fullscreen { justify-content: center; ... overflow-y: auto; } (reader.module.css:521-529) on the flex column .reader. In the reading view the column (tools, five sheets, closing) is taller than the screen, so centring pushes the overflow above the start edge, where a scroll container cannot scroll. t13.mjs/t13.json, full screen then «عرض للقراءة»: at 1440x900 scrollTop 0, page 1 top at -2563px, «عرض الكتاب» and «الخروج من ملء الشاشة» at -2631px, scrollTo(0) changes nothing; at 390x794 page 1 at -920px, buttons at -988px. Focus sits on «عرض الكتاب» off screen. Screenshot t13-w1440-fs-reading-top.png shows the bottom of page 3 at the very top of the scroll range.
impact: A visitor who reads in full screen and switches to the reading view cannot see the dedication, the first introduction page or the controls, including the button to leave full screen; only Esc (or the system back gesture) gets them out, and they never read pages 1-3 in that view.
proposed_fix: Use overflow-safe alignment: .reader:fullscreen { justify-content: safe center; } (or keep flex-start and centre the book stage with margin-block: auto on its first and last children). Add an e2e step: full screen, «عرض للقراءة», expect the first sheet and «عرض الكتاب» to be reachable (toBeInViewport after scrolling the full-screen element to the top).
prior_overlap: none: the e2e full-screen test only enters and leaves full screen in the book view

title: In full screen the reading view draws a page only once it is on screen: no look-ahead, blank paper while scrolling
evidence: The IntersectionObserver has the viewport as root with rootMargin 100% 0px (StaticPdfReader.tsx:33-46). In full screen the sheets scroll inside .reader:fullscreen (overflow-y: auto), whose clip the root margin does not extend. t12.json: in the page, page 2 is drawn while 1655px down (look-ahead works); in full screen page 4 at 914px (just under the 900px screen) stays blank, and after scrolling 1000px page 5 at 1073px is blank, both drawn only once they enter.
impact: Reading in full screen, each page shows as plain paper for the moment it takes to render as it scrolls in (more visible on a slow phone).
proposed_fix: Observe with the scrolling element as root when there is one: pass root: document.fullscreenElement ?? null (re-create the observer on fullscreenchange, e.g. key the effect on a fullscreen prop from PdfBookReader).

title: docs/book-preview.md says a key pressed during a turn is ignored; the reader queues it
evidence: Line 64: "A key pressed while a page is still turning is ignored". The code stores the last move in pendingRef while page-flip is flipping and replays it at rest (PdfBookReader.tsx:211-213, 231-233, 372-381; the comment at 133-135 says so). t14.mjs: ArrowLeft, then ArrowLeft 150 ms later during the turn: the labels went «المقدمة 2 / 5» then «3–4 / 5».
impact: Whoever maintains the reader (or writes its tests) is told the opposite of what the code does; a test written from the doc would fail or, worse, the queue would be removed as a bug.
proposed_fix: Replace the sentence with: "A key pressed while a page is still turning is kept, and the last one is made once the turn ends."
prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 BOOK-1 changed the behaviour (queue instead of stacking); the doc was not updated

title: The e2e test meant to prove pdf.js stays out of the first load cannot see the pdf.js or page-flip chunks
evidence: expect(urls.filter((url) => /.pdf$|pdf.worker|page-flip/.test(url))).toEqual([]) (reader.spec.ts:103). In the export the chunks are content-hashed: pdf.js is /_next/static/chunks/11ph49ml3gu1-.js and page-flip /_next/static/chunks/3y7oy_tt71u1t.js (t1.json afterOpenRequests); neither name matches the regex. Only the worker and the PDF, which are requested by getDocument, are caught. Today the invariant holds (t1.json initialJs has neither chunk), but a static import of pdfjs-dist into the page would still pass this test.
impact: D10 (lazy load) can regress silently: the visitor of /book would download about 433 KB of pdf.js (plus page-flip) up front, and the test meant to guard it stays green.
proposed_fix: Assert on content, not names: before opening, collect the script responses (page.on(response) for resourceType script) and expect none of their bodies to contain GlobalWorkerOptions (pdf.js) or stf__parent (page-flip); after opening, expect a newly loaded script to contain GlobalWorkerOptions.

title: The phone reading view never redraws for pinch zoom: the zoom its own hint asks for magnifies a 2x bitmap
evidence: drawNear() draws each sheet at host.clientWidth with the default maxDpr 2 (pdf.ts:149-151); only an IntersectionObserver and a ResizeObserver trigger it, and neither fires on pinch zoom (no visualViewport use in src/components/book). The hint under the tools says «كبّر الصفحة بإصبعين لقراءة أوضح.». t18.mjs, 360x780 DPR 3, reading view, CDP page scale 3: visualViewport.scale 3, the page 1 canvas stays 640x800 for a 320px sheet, so each canvas pixel covers 4.5 screen pixels; t18-pinch3x.png shows the page text soft and stair-stepped next to the crisp HTML text of the sticky nav. The book text is about 6.9 CSS px on a phone (t3.json phone_bookFont), so zooming is the only way to read it.
impact: On a phone, the only way to read Anas pages comfortably is to pinch, and the result is visibly blurred Arabic (dots and harakat soften), on the device most visitors use.
proposed_fix: In StaticPdfReader, listen to visualViewport resize (debounced, e.g. on gesture end) and redraw the near sheets with maxDpr = min(devicePixelRatio * visualViewport.scale, 4); PageSurface keys its cache on width@dpr, so only a real change redraws. Keep the 2x default when not zoomed.

title: On viewports taller than about 1440px the boards, the closed-book centring and the focus ring are sized for pages page-flip never draws
evidence: The stage assumes a page 0.8 x --stage-h wide (--stage-h: min(78svh, 62.5cqi), --page-w: calc(var(--stage-h) * 0.8), reader.module.css:21-23), but page-flip caps a page at maxWidth: 900 (PdfBookReader.tsx:295), i.e. 900x1125. t19.mjs/t19.json: at 2560x1600 the stage is 1248px high, the pages 900x1125 and the .case boards 2021x1272 (thick saffron margins round the block, t19-w2560-open.png); closed, the cover centre is at 1329 against a stage centre of 1280. At 3840x2160 the boards are 2720x1709 round an 1800x1125 block and the closed cover is 224px right of centre, with the focus ring drawn round the assumed 1348px page (t19-w3840-closed.png).
impact: Visitors on large monitors at low scaling (for example 4K at 100% or 3072x1728) see the book in an oversized saffron frame and, closed, off centre, unlike the designed thin hardcover boards.
proposed_fix: Cap the stage at page-flip own maximum: --stage-h: min(78svh, 62.5cqi, 1125px) (and the same 1125px term in the full-screen rule), so --page-w never exceeds 900; or raise page-flip maxWidth to cover the largest stage.
